The refactor is complete and verified. Here's what I did and why.

## What the upcoming change needs

The change caps a new owner's `membershipLevel` at *one above the maximum among their household members*. That makes `membershipLevel` — currently a **pure self-derived getter** on `Owner` — depend on *other owners*, which only the controller's creation pipeline can see. In this codebase, every value derived at creation from other owners (`customerCode`, `namesakeCount`, `householdSize`, `possibleDuplicate`) is a **stored field assigned in `assignDerivedAttributes` via a per-attribute `x(owner)` method**. So `membershipLevel` needs to move into that same shape, and the pipeline needs a clean way to reach an owner's household members.

## Preparation (behaviour-preserving, no cap implemented)

**`Owner.java`**
- Added a persisted `membership_level` field, grouped with the other creation-derived attributes.
- Split `getMembershipLevel()`: it is now the **stored accessor**, falling back to the point-based derivation when no level is assigned (so seed data / non-pipeline owners return exactly what they returned before). Added `setMembershipLevel(...)`.
- The point→level logic is unchanged, relocated to `getBaseMembershipLevel()` — the value the pipeline starts from.

**`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`**
- `assignDerivedAttributes` now assigns `owner.setMembershipLevel(membershipLevel(owner))`, exactly matching the existing `owner.setX(x(owner))` pattern. `membershipLevel(Owner)` currently returns the base level (no cap) — this is the single method the change will edit.
- Extracted `householdMembers(String householdId)` as the **single source of a household's existing membership**, following the codebase's "never re-derive elsewhere" idiom. `isHouseholdDuplicate` now routes through it, and it's the seam the cap will use to read household members' levels.

**Schemas** — added `membership_level` to all four dialect `schema.sql` files (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres), matching each dialect's column style.

## Behaviour preserved / tests

For any owner, `getMembershipLevel()` returns the same number as before (created owners store the base level; others fall back to computing it). `isHouseholdDuplicate` is logically identical (`anyMatch` → `!isEmpty()`).

One caveat worth stating plainly: the sole test in the repo, `AcceptanceTest.coreCapsLevelByHousehold`, is the **acceptance test for the upcoming change and is already red** — it creates a second same-household owner without `sharesHousehold`, which the existing duplicate rule rejects with `409`. The refactor is complete and verified. Here's what I did and why.

## What the upcoming change needs

The change caps a new owner's `membershipLevel` at *one above the maximum among their household members*. That makes `membershipLevel` — currently a **pure self-derived getter** on `Owner` — depend on *other owners*, which only the controller's creation pipeline can see. In this codebase, every value derived at creation from other owners (`customerCode`, `namesakeCount`, `householdSize`, `possibleDuplicate`) is a **stored field assigned in `assignDerivedAttributes` via a per-attribute `x(owner)` method**. So `membershipLevel` needs to move into that same shape, and the pipeline needs a clean way to reach an owner's household members.

## Preparation (behaviour-preserving, no cap implemented)

**`Owner.java`**
- Added a persisted `membership_level` field, grouped with the other creation-derived attributes.
- Split `getMembershipLevel()`: it is now the **stored accessor**, falling back to the point-based derivation when no level is assigned (so seed data / non-pipeline owners return exactly what they returned before). Added `setMembershipLevel(...)`.
- The point→level logic is unchanged, relocated to `getBaseMembershipLevel()` — the value the pipeline starts from.

**`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`**
- `assignDerivedAttributes` now assigns `owner.setMembershipLevel(membershipLevel(owner))`, exactly matching the existing `owner.setX(x(owner))` pattern. `membershipLevel(Owner)` currently returns the base level (no cap) — this is the single method the change will edit.
- Extracted `householdMembers(String householdId)` as the **single source of a household's existing membership**, following the codebase's "never re-derive elsewhere" idiom. `isHouseholdDuplicate` now routes through it, and it's the seam the cap will use to read household members' levels.

**Schemas** — added `membership_level` to all four dialect `schema.sql` files (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres), matching each dialect's column style.

## Behaviour preserved / tests

For any owner, `getMembershipLevel()` returns the same number as before (created owners store the base level; others fall back to computing it). `isHouseholdDuplicate` is logically identical (`anyMatch` → `!isEmpty()`).

One caveat worth stating plainly: the sole test in the repo, `AcceptanceTest.coreCapsLevelByHousehold`, is the **acceptance test for the upcoming change and is already red** — it creates a second same-household owner without `sharesHousehold`, which the existing duplicate rule rejects with `409`. I did **not** make it green, because that requires implementing the change (explicitly out of scope). I confirmed my refactor leaves it failing at the *identical* point (line 21, `409`) with no new error — in particular owner `a` is created successfully, proving the new persisted column works end-to-end. No previously-passing behaviour was broken.

With this in place, implementing the cap is a one-method edit to `membershipLevel(Owner)`:

```java
int base = owner.getBaseMembershipLevel();
return householdMembers(owner.getHouseholdId()).stream()
    .map(Owner::getMembershipLevel).max(Integer::compare)
    .map(max -> Math.min(base, max + 1))
    .orElse(base);
